items.title: George Avakian interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, April 21, 1998
items.q: Michael and his assistant George Arevelo are very happy to show people around

ctx.x: Yeah. He must have had an incredible energy also, because I did visit there and when you look at all the things he did with his tapes you know, just decorating the boxes and all that, like he was never without something to do.

That’s right. He was always busy. And one of the things that kind of shocked me after he showed me more of his things than I’d seen before was that he had acquired this scotch tape which came in big sheets, and he would put those big sheets of scotch tape over photographs and everything. And my brother finally told him, “You know Pops, you’ve got to stop using this because the material that makes it adhesive is very harmful to the surface of photographs for example, and you will never be able to peel things away…
To take this idea into a kind of a current aspect, this kind of racial divisions that happened, sometimes not from the musicians but from outside. What do you see is the racial outlook of jazz today?
